## (1) First message

**Premise correction.** The ticket's second row assumes the export can include an owner column. The table contract has no owner column: `src/export/csv.ts:40` defines `const tableColumns = ["title", "status"];`, and per the gather draft, the CSV exporter reuses these table column definitions. If the export reuses the table columns unchanged, it cannot satisfy the owner row. The design proceeds on the corrected fact that the column set is title and status only. You can override this in your reply.

**Framing check.** The framing holds. I checked:
- The column list at `src/export/csv.ts:40`.
- The data path from the table's column definitions into the CSV exporter, which is the only consumer the ask's constraints name.
- The draft's finding that the reports page renders a table with no export action, so nothing already solves this.

I found no case that the ask is misdiagnosed, wrong-sized, or a band-aid.

**Unverified.** These tools were not used, so I could not verify from primary code:
- Whether report rows carry an owner field at all.
- How the page component is structured.

These go to Open Questions.

**Ticket scope.** The ticket is acme/widgets#77, with an unheaded checkbox list and no repo groups. All three rows belong to this repo (`acme/widgets`).

The owner row contradicts the column contract the exporter reuses. How should that row ship?

- **A) in-scope.** The export uses the table's columns plus an appended owner column, read from each report row. The on-screen table stays unchanged.
- **B) deviates:** \<why\>
- **C) deferred:** \<where\>
- **D) repair the ticket.** Run `/skill:shape-ticket acme/widgets#77 "The export includes the owner column." - src/export/csv.ts:40 table columns are title and status only.`

**Recommendation: A.** The row can still ship in this gauntlet if report rows carry an owner value. Only the reused column list needs widening, and only for export. If the report data has no owner field, switch to D.

## (2) Approaches message

**Premises.**
- **Corrected:** The exportable columns today are title and status (`src/export/csv.ts:40`). There is no owner column.
- **Supported:** The page has no export action. The CSV exporter reuses the table's column definitions (gather draft, `csv.ts`).
- **Unverified:** Whether report rows expose an owner value. Also unverified is whether the existing paging can produce a 10k-row export in under 60s. I ran no measurement. Both are Open Questions. The 60s row stays in-scope with a 10k-row fixture test named in Design.

**Settled so far.**
- The button sits beside the report title, per your answer.
- No reply to the owner-row question is recorded. That row therefore stays in-scope (the default) under reading A: table columns plus owner, export-only.

**The axis** is where the export's column set and execution live. They can stay coupled to the table or run as a separate export pipeline.

**Recommended: reuse the existing CSV serializer and paging, with an export-only column extension.**
- The new button calls the existing serializer.
- The serializer pages through the report with the current paging.
- The serializer writes `[...tableColumns, "owner"]` as its header and fields.
- The extension is derived in `csv.ts`, so the table definition stays the single source for title and status.
- This adds no new construct beyond one derived list and a button handler. It is also the reuse-only candidate.
- **Pattern:** Follows the column reuse at `src/export/csv.ts:40`. It extends the list rather than forking it, so the table and export cannot drift on shared columns.

**Alternative: add owner to the table contract itself.**
- `tableColumns` gains owner, so the page and the export keep one list.
- This is simpler for the exporter but changes the on-screen table, which no ticket row asks for.
- **Pattern:** Keeps the one-list coupling at `src/export/csv.ts:40` intact. It widens the UI's scope beyond the ask.

**Alternative: server-side background export job.**
- This drops the ask's implicit assumption that the export runs synchronously from the page.
- A job builds the file and the button downloads it when the job completes. That makes the 60s bound robust even if paging is slow.
- It adds a new job/queue boundary.
- **Pattern:** Cuts across the existing synchronous serializer-and-paging path in `src/export/csv.ts`, creating a second export path beside it.

**Flip condition.** If a 10k-row fixture run of the existing paging exceeds 60s, I would switch to the background-job approach. If report rows have no owner field, the owner row goes back to the cut question (option D) before either approach proceeds.

D) **repair the ticket** — run `/skill:shape-ticket acme/widgets#77` to reconcile the owner requirement with the current column contract.

**Recommendation: A — the ticket expressly requires owner; the current implementation lacking it is not, by itself, a reason to drop the requirement.**
